account: Today has mostly been routine mayoral business: office work, a market walk, and tea with the neighbour at the dockside cottage. The secretary had to find and confirm the tea host because the appointment book originally lacked a precise address. The neighbour welcomed me and seemed well. The only unusual report was the neighbour's vague rumour about a bridge or port change. They had not seen evidence themselves, and the secretary has received neither correspondence nor a confirmed proposal about it. I do not know whether there is any actual change planned, who might be behind it, or what purpose it would serve. I asked that the rumour not be treated as fact. The secretary checked the office chest and returned the original appointment book, tea confirmation, and grain inspection brief; there was no new correspondence requiring a decision. I have reached home just after my scheduled nineteen hundred return. Tomorrow I need to review the appointments at the office at eight and attend the mill's grain inspection at ten. I have not yet read the inspection brief.
